FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 472
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Representative Chris Pringle
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 04/23/2024
House Bill 472 as introduce would increase the maximum compensation that certain district
attorneys retired under the Employees’ Retirement System (ERS)may earn, without suspension
of their retirement allowance, through returning to work part-time, provided that the
compensation does not exceed $50,000 commencing October 1, 2024.
This bill would increase the obligations of district attorneys that employ such retirees by an
undetermined amount dependent upon any additional compensation paid to such retiree under
the provisions of this act.
This bill would also increase the obligations of the ERS by an undetermined amount dependent
upon the number of employees that retire and return to work and earn compensation above the
current retiree compensation cap but less than the proposed new maximum of $50,000 but who
would not otherwise have retired and received retirement benefits absent the provisions of this
bill.
This bill would also further increase the obligations of the ERS by an undetermined amount
dependent on any additional creditable service awarded for rural incentive time to certain
assistant district attorneys employed in a certain judicial circuit.
This bill would also further increase the obligations of the ERS by an undetermined amount
dependent on the difference in: (1) Tier I retirement benefits received by certain district attorney
employees pursuant to this bill; and (2) Tier II benefits otherwise received under current law.
These obligations could be offset, in whole or in part, by increased employee contributions at a
rate of 7.5% of the employee's compensation received by the ERS pursuant to this bill.
